turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_te_zt900_train.csv: 300 real samples, columns process/composition
    columns (O, Sb, Co, Si, Sn, Ca, Ni, Ti, Pb, Se, Ge, Cu, Zr, Te, S, Zn,
    Fe, Yb, Mn, Sr, Nb, Bi, Cd, Hf, In) and `target` (the measured zT
    (thermoelectric figure of merit) at 900 K).
  - b3_te_zt900_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE samples whose zT (thermoelectric
    figure of merit) at 900 K was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST zT
(thermoelectric figure of merit) at 900 K, then select the 5 best candidates
from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the training data

**Which chemistries reach the highest zT (900 K) in the training set?**

| Family | Signature | Observed zT |
|---|---|---|
| PbTe (+S, +Se, +Sr) | Pb≈0.48–0.49, Te 0.35–0.61 | **1.9 – 2.26** (top of dataset) |
| Cu₂₋ₓSe | Cu≈0.64–0.67, Se≈0.32–0.33 | **1.17 – 1.74** (higher as Cu/Se sum drops below 1) |
| PbSe / PbSe–S | Pb≈0.48–0.50, Se 0.42–0.50 | 0.85 – 1.62 |
| (Zr,Hf)NiSn half-Heusler | Sn≈0.33, Ni≈0.33, Zr≈0.13, Hf≈0.20, no/low Ti | 0.95 – 1.35 (Ti substitution *hurts*: Ti≥0.15 → 0.3–0.6) |
| PbS, FeNbSb(Ti), Yb₁₄MnSb₁₁ | — | 0.7 – 1.1 |
| Oxides (O-rich: CaMnO₃, SrTiO₃, ZnO, Ca₃Co₄O₉) | O≈0.5–0.75 | mostly < 0.35 |

Key rules extracted: (i) high Te with Pb is the single strongest positive signal; (ii) Cu–Se (Cu:Se ≈ 2, slightly Cu-deficient) is second; (iii) oxide-rich rows are always poor; (iv) in half-Heuslers, Zr/Hf co-alloying without Ti is best; (v) PbTe doped only with Bi/Sb stays modest (0.68–0.89), it is the S/Se/Sr-containing PbTe that explodes to >2.

**Applying to the pool**

- **c052** (Pb 0.493 / Te 0.394 / S 0.099) is nearly identical to the train point Pb 0.494/Te 0.346/S 0.148 → zT = 2.21, and sits in the PbTe–S region that dominates the top of the dataset. Best bet (~2).
- **c054** (Cu 0.651 / Se 0.326, sum 0.977) lies between train Cu₂Se points 0.99 → 1.45 and 0.955 → 1.74 → predicted ~1.5–1.7.
- **c063** (Cu 0.664 / Se 0.336, sum 1.0) matches the stoichiometric Cu₂Se points → ~1.2.
- **c078** (Sb 0.003 / Sn 0.33 / Ni 0.333 / Zr 0.133 / Hf 0.20, **no Ti**) is the exact optimal half-Heusler window (train analogues 0.95, 1.01, 1.32, 1.35) → ~1.1–1.3.
- **c012** (Pb 0.50 / Se 0.498) — the PbSe family is consistently ≥1.1 in training (0.85–1.62) → ~1.0.

Close runners-up considered and ranked below: c035/c093 (half-Heusler, Zr/Hf but slightly off-optimum), c097/c025 (SnTe-based), c006/c041/c001 (PbTe with only Bi doping — training says ~0.7–0.9), and the FeNbSb–Ti group (c034, c023, c095 ≈ 0.9–1.0).

Oxide-heavy candidates (c003, c017–c022, c029, c047, c064, c076, c079, c081, c092 …) are predicted low and excluded.

**Final: c052, c054, c054→c063, c078, c012**

Final: c052, c054, c063, c078, c012
